title: Counting down with range()
description: A for loop that uses a negative step to iterate in reverse order.

original.hint: A negative step means range() counts downward. Where does it start, and when does it stop?
walkthrough: range(3, 0, -1) starts at 3 and decreases by 1 on each iteration.
It stops before reaching the stop value of 0 — so 0 itself is never visited.
On each iteration i holds the current value in the descending sequence.
The loop ends when the next step would equal or go past the stop value.

mutation.code:
for i in range(3, 0, -1):
    print(i * i)
mutation.diff_description: Applies a multiplicative expression to i before printing.
mutation.hint: The sequence of values i takes is identical to the original. What changes is the expression used to compute what gets printed.
walkthrough: range(3, 0, -1) produces the same descending sequence as before.
On each iteration, the printed value is computed by applying an expression to i.
Trace that expression for each value of i in the sequence.

transfer.code:
result = []
for i in range(3, 0, -1):
    result.append(i)
print(result)
transfer.hint: Instead of printing on each iteration, the loop is collecting values into a list. What will the list contain after all iterations complete?
walkthrough: result starts as an empty list before the loop.
On each iteration, the current value of i is appended to result.
The loop visits the same sequence of values as the original exercise.
After all iterations, result holds every value that was appended, in order.
print(result) outputs the entire list once, after the loop ends.
